rationale_one_line: Shen-Backpressure is a typed-Lisp + compiler thesis with a bold opinionated claim, which is exactly what MANIFESTO is for; mono-terminal (matrix-green on near-black, JetBrainsMono, cut motion) is the native register for formal-methods builders and the only preset out of the 14-entry lookback window.
writing_tone_notes: Essayistic-engineer. No superlatives. Plain declaratives. Lower-case everything (mono-terminal preset enforces case: lower). Contractions where natural. Short sentences. The contrast carries the praise — the thesis is the flattery.
do_rules: Render every scene in JetBrainsMono on near-black canvas with matrix-green accent.
Use both flash scenes as the visual heroes — one bold word per beat, all lowercase.
Land the thesis on the first flash; land the result on the second.
Let the close subtitle name a different angle (language footprint) than the X caption.
Camera moves: orbit on title, crash_zoom on both flashes, push_in on fix, pull_back on close — four distinct moves with the required orbit.
dont_rules: Don't repeat 'structural backpressure beats smarter agents' inside scene copy (the X caption owns that quote).
Don't repeat 'the model has to satisfy' inside scene copy.
Don't introduce a serif body — mono-terminal is one font.
Don't claim MIT or any specific license — the repo ships no LICENSE file.
Don't claim Shen is a 1970s language — Shen itself is recent; sequent calculus is the older substrate.
